learning_outcomes.text: Knows the friction processes in mechanical systems specific to mechanical systems under various operating conditions.
Knows the use of adequate lubricants and lubrication processes specific to gears, plain bearings, rolling bearings, joints, etc.
Knows the wear processes in mechanical systems and how to reduce them.
Knows the methods for estimating the reliability of mechanical systems, in relation to tribological safety criteria correlated with complex friction, wear, and lubrication processes.
Knows how to use tribological safety criteria in the conception and design of mechanical systems.
Uses test benches to observe and monitor phenomena of friction, wear, and lubrication.
Interprets the influence of various factors on friction, wear, and lubrication processes.
Calculates friction forces and moments as well as power consumed by friction.
Calculates stress states in punctual, linear, or surface friction pairs.
Calculates film thicknesses for various operating conditions and for various lubricants.
Recognizes various types of lubricants and their purpose.
Recognizes various wear phenomena and their causes.
Knows tribological safety criteria and can apply them in the design and operation of mechanical systems.
Knows the use of software for monitoring tribological processes.

Respects the principles, norms, and ethical values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group, applies relational techniques and efficient work in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents oneself in their field of activity by adequately using effective methods and techniques for lifelong learning.
Develops professional projects in the field of mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Tribology - science of friction, wear and lubrication processes in tribosystems. Tribotechnics - science of applying tribological concepts in the design and construction of machines and industrial equipment.

Friction pairs - tribosystems - industrial applications. Identification of tribosystems in various mechanical systems specific to automobiles, mechatronic structures, thermal equipment, processing industry equipment, etc.

The role of mechanical processing in obtaining real contact surfaces specific to friction pairs. Types of mechanical processing and obtained roughnesses. Real surfaces and topographical elements useful for the study of tribological processes. Real contact areas.

Applications of rolling contact stresses in rolling bearings, gears, rolling guides, cam-follower mechanisms, railway wheels. Ideal surfaces. Specific geometric elements (curvature, curvature function, equivalent radii of curvature). Hertzian contacts; Basic relationships in the calculation of contact pressures. Calculation examples.

Evaluation of friction losses in tribosystems. Estimation of friction losses in sliding and rolling. Applications to plain bearings, rolling bearings, and gears. Estimation of efficiency in tribosystems.

Lubricants and lubrication methods used in mechanical engineering; Oils, consistent greases; Solid lubricants. Lubrication methods used: splash lubrication, oil jet lubrication, oil mist lubrication, gas lubrication, etc.

Hydrodynamic lubrication (HD) applied to radial and axial plain bearings; HD load capacity; Flow rates and minimum film thickness; Friction in HD films; Thermal effects; Geometric and functional optimization of radial plain bearings in HD regime.
Hydrostatic lubrication (HS) applied to sliding guides and axial and radial bearings. Design of lubrication systems, selection of lubricants, determination of necessary oil flow rates.

Elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHD) applied to rolling bearings, gears, ball screws, etc. Determination of the minimum lubricant film thickness and correlation with surface roughness; Influence of lubrication on the durability of rolling bearings and gears.

Methods and techniques for reducing wear in tribosystems. Methods for reducing adhesive wear and preventing seizing in gears through additive lubricants; Methods for reducing abrasive wear - correct choices of lubricants, roughnesses and adequate seals; Reduction of contact fatigue wear in rolling bearings, gears, etc.; Reduction of corrosion wear.
Design of tribosystems according to tribological safety criteria.
Determination of contact pressures and deformations in rolling tribosystems. Applications to rolling bearings, gears, ball screws, rolling guides.
Experimental determination of friction coefficients on sliding and rolling tribomodels, under dry, boundary, and mixed friction conditions on the AMSLER Machine and CETR UMT2 Tribometer.
Testing of high-pressure resistance characteristics of oils on the 4-ball machine. Comparative tests with oils having various additive grades.
Optimized design of a plain bearing with respect to the minimum lubricant film thickness and the operating temperature. Applications to industrial bearings.
Determination of lubrication regimes with applications to rolling bearings, gears, ball screws, rolling guides.
Study of adhesion (seizing) and abrasion wear processes on tribomodels with sliding and rolling motion using the AMSLER Machine. Applications in gears.
Estimation of industrial machinery reliability in relation to wear processes. Applications to gears: determination of the risk of seizing on tooth flanks.

Presentations of demonstration sequences for relationships and calculation examples
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of associated study credits. For the exam, evaluation methods include systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments to be completed between courses, preparation of a case study report), a formative evaluation test during the semester, and a final summative evaluation test. For the laboratory, evaluation includes completing all laboratory work (allowing recovery of only one missed laboratory work) and a laboratory colloquium evaluation test.
